heading.en: Every credit bill in one place

hook.en: A stationery wholesaler buys from twenty suppliers on credit every week. One book lists all these bills; another lists the goods sent back.
hook.kn: ಒಬ್ಬ ಸಗಟು ವ್ಯಾಪಾರಿ ಪ್ರತಿ ವಾರ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು ಪೂರೈಕೆದಾರರಿಂದ ಸಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಖರೀದಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಒಂದು ಪುಸ್ತಕ ಈ ಬಿಲ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು, ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ವಾಪಸ್ ಕಳುಹಿಸಿದ ಸರಕನ್ನು ದಾಖಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: A stationery wholesaler buys from twenty suppliers on credit every week. One book lists all these bills; another lists the goods sent back. In this lesson: Prepare a purchases book.
Prepare a purchases return book.
Post them to the ledger.

body.en: The *purchases* book records only credit purchases of goods meant for resale. Its columns are Date, Invoice number, Name of supplier (particulars), L.F. and Amount; trade discount is deducted in the details and only the net amount is entered. Each supplier's account is credited with the amount, and the periodic total is debited to Purchases Account. Cash purchases go to the cash book and credit purchases of assets to the journal proper.
body.kn: ಖರೀದಿ ಪುಸ್ತಕದಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾರಾಟಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಸಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೊಂಡ ಸರಕು ಮಾತ್ರ ದಾಖಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿ ಪೂರೈಕೆದಾರನ ಖಾತೆ ಕ್ರೆಡಿಟ್, ಒಟ್ಟು ಮೊತ್ತ ಖರೀದಿ ಖಾತೆಗೆ ಡೆಬಿಟ್.

say.en: Let us work this out step by step. Record in the purchases book of Vidya Book House, August 2025: Aug 3 bought from Gupta Bros 100 notebooks at 40 rupees less 10 percent trade discount; Aug 10 bought from Sharma Traders 50 pens at 20 rupees; Aug 15 bought a computer on credit from Tech World 35,000 rupees.
Gupta Bros: 100 times 40 rupees equals 4,000 rupees less 10 percent 400 rupees equals 3,600 rupees.
Sharma Traders: 50 times 20 rupees equals 1,000 rupees.
The computer is an asset, not goods for resale: it goes to the journal proper, not the purchases book.
Total of purchases book equals 3,600 plus 1,000 equals 4,600, rupees debited to Purchases A over c; Gupta Bros credited 3,600 rupees and Sharma Traders 1,000 rupees.
So the answer is Purchases book total 4,600 rupees.
